newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sells 5.25 bln reais in Treasury papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sells 5.25 bln reais in Treasury papers.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank, on behalf of the National Treasury, raised 5.25 billion reais during an auction of Treasury Notes and Letters, dealers said.
A total of 3.493 billion reais was sold in two series of National Treasury Letters known as LTNs.
A total of 2.262 billion reais of 181-day LTNs, due in July 1 1997, was sold at an overnight call money rate of 2.4858 percent a month.
The Central Bank also sold 1.231 billion reais of 365-day LTNs, due in January 1 1998, at a call money rate of 2.35 percent a month.
Some 1.036 billion reais were sold in National Treasury Notes (NTN) indexed to the variation of Brazil's reference rate (TR).
The notes, which are due in July 1 1997, pay annual yields of 12.85 percent plus the variation of the TR in the maturity period.

The Central Bank sold a series of NTNs indexed to the variation of the dollar, known as NTN-D. A total of 721 million reais in NTN-D with a maturity period of two years will pay annual yields of 11.93 percent, dealers said.
